newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end over one percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end over one percent higher.

text.p: Swiss shares ended more than one percent higher on Tuesday in a steady rise, profiting from a strong Wall Street and firming bond futures.
The market was expecting the U.S. Fed to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at a meeting the same day of the policy making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), one dealer said.
Volume was described as low ahaed of the long Easter holiday weekend. Further development was seen depending on the outcome of the FOMC meeting.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 61.3 points or 1.36 percent to 4,558.6 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index up 31.18 points or 1.09 percent to 2,887.96.
CS Group and Novartis were among the biggest gainers. CS Group powered ahead 6.50 francs, or 3.9 percent, to end at 173.
Novartis registereds, up 46 francs to 1,760, were reportedly bolstered by switches from Roche.
Roche was easier after announcing a 16 percent rise in 1996 net profit to 3.899 billion Swiss francs on Monday.

Nestle climbed six francs to 1,577. The company is due to release 1996 results on Wednesday. According to market consensus, Nestle is likely to report a net profit increase of 10.5 percent to around 3.23 billion Swiss francs.
Several stocks were seen making up for recent losses. Among them were insurers Swiss Re and Zurich and temporary employment group Adecco, which added between two and three percent.
Stocks of goods inspection firm Surveillance continued their recent fall, giving up 80 francs to 2,950. The shares were pulled down by a sell recommendation, traders said.
Alusuisse, Holderbank and Winterthur were also among the losers.
